newsitem.title: USA: Florida lawmaker to fend off Republican challenge.
newsitem.headline: Florida lawmaker to fend off Republican challenge.

text.p: Florida House Majority Leader Jim Davis has won the right to fend off a Republican challenger for the U.S. House seat being vacated by retiring 17-term Democratic Congressman Sam Gibbons, election officials confirmed Wednesday.
Davis, 38, defeated former Tampa Mayor Sandy Freedman, 52, who had been considerd the front-runner, in a runoff election Tuesday to choose the Democrat on the November ballot.
Election officials said Wednesday that, when all precincts had reported, Davis won with 56 percent, or 23,626 votes, to Freedman's 44 percent, or 18,418.
Turnout was light, with only about 40,000 votes being cast, or less than 20 percent of eligible voters.
Gibbons' 11th District House seat was seen as the most vulnerable to a Republican takeover of the three open House seats in Florida.
Freedman asked her supporters to work for him in the Nov. 5 contest against Republican Mark Sharpe, 36.

Sharpe, a private school teacher, was nominated without opposition. He ran against Gibbons in 1992 and 1994, losing both times, but coming near an upset in 1994. Sharpe's previous campaigns, based on balancing the federal budget, have made him familiar to voters.
Gibbons, who represented Tampa for 17 terms, is retiring at the end of the current term.
